Subject: BrightHealth MAP: Maestro evaluation plan + sandbox access

Emily / Mike —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a condensed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that covers the performance evaluation scope, acceptance criteria, and a tentative close timeline. Highlights:

- Evaluation environment: Redwood Dedicated sandbox (us-west-2) with isolated project and telemetry. We will provide temporary API keys and a read-only view in Console.
- Test harness: standard load driver + synthetic user prompts + three representative datasets you shared (claims summarization, member Q&A, clinical triage).
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency (ms), TTFT (time-to-first-token, ms), steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), max sustainable concurrency, and QA accuracy (exact match / ROUGE-L).
- Target SLOs you requested: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 300ms, TTFT < 80ms, support concurrency 16 QPS with <10% p95 SLA degradation.
- Model variants to evaluate (from Redwood catalog): rw-3b-int8, rw-13b-q4, rw-70b-8q (we can swap in other candidates if you prefer).

Deliverables & timeline (proposed):
1) Sandbox + MAP workbook shared (today) — attachment: 20261110_bh_map_maestro_v1.xlsx
2) Data ingest & baseline runs (2 business days) — expected: Nov 12
3) Full perf sweep + quality eval (3 business days) — expected: Nov 16
4) Exec demo & decision meeting (Nov 19)
5) Procurement & contract signature (target Nov 24)

Please confirm the datasets we'll use for quality scoring (I attached the sample list in the workbook) and call out any additional constraints (PII handling, retention window).

I'll spin up the sandbox and send credentials via a secure link by EOD.

— Diego

Subject: FW: BrightHealth MAP — preliminary perf sweep results (internal)

Team —

I ran the initial perf + quality sweep this weekend against the BrightHealth sample sets. Results attached (maestro_perf_results_v2.csv). High-level summary below — please review and add comments in the drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/BH-MAESTRO-2026

Quick summary (single-node, A100s, 1x model worker, synthetic steady-state load):
- rw-3b-int8:
  - p50: 34ms, p95: 90ms, TTFT: 28ms
  - throughput (tokens/sec): 1,100 (at concurrency 8, batch size 8)
  - QA exact match: 68%, ROUGE-L: 0.41
  - Notes: excellent latency/cost; fails to meet accuracy threshold for Q&A (target 80%).

- rw-13b-q4:
  - p50: 88ms, p95: 260ms, TTFT: 62ms
  - throughput (tokens/sec): 520 (concurrency 12, batch size 6)
  - QA exact match: 81%, ROUGE-L: 0.57
  - Notes: meets quality targets and within SLOs marginally; higher resource use.

- rw-70b-8q:
  - p50: 320ms, p95: 1100ms, TTFT: 220ms
  - throughput (tokens/sec): 210 (concurrency 4, batch size 4)
  - QA exact match: 88%, ROUGE-L: 0.68
  - Notes: best quality but fails latency and concurrency SLOs for the use case. Requires multi-node sharding to approach targets, which increases cost and complexity.

Cost/operational notes:
- rw-3b-int8 is ~0.45x the infra cost of rw-13b-q4 for the same token volume given the higher token/s and smaller memory footprint.
- rw-13b-q4 is the sweet spot for BrightHealth's Q&A workload: meets the 80% QA target and with batching/TTFT tuning can meet the p95 <= 300ms target in Dedicated with a 2-worker pool.
- rw-70b-8q will require dedicated multi-GPU deployment and will push procurement toward enterprise contract terms.

Next suggested actions before the Nov 19 demo:
1) Run a 2-worker rw-13b-q4 config with prefix caching enabled and automated batching tuned to your real request distribution. Expect p95 to tighten to ~220–240ms.
2) Run a short inference cost projection for 3, 6, 12 month horizons.
3) Prep a short slide showing tradeoffs (latency vs QA vs cost) — I can draft.

Attaching maestro_perf_results_v2.csv. Feedback welcome.

— Diego
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FW: BrightHealth MAP — preliminary perf sweep results (internal)

Nice work — quick operational notes from infra/console POV: 

- Deployment recommendation: rw-13b-q4 on Dedicated with a 2-worker pool + autoscaling policy (scale up at 70% CPU/GPU util, scale down after 3m idle). Enable prefix/KV caching for session-heavy Q&A to reduce tail latency.
- Batching knobs: increase batch max to 12 for steady state; adaptive batching covers short bursts and keeps TTFT low. Expect ~1.2x throughput improvement vs current run.
- Observability: enable token-level tracing and per-route latency heatmaps for the demo so BrightHealth can see tail behavior during the exec demo.
- Cost ballpark: ~ $6.5k/month per 2-worker rw-13b-q4 pool on Dedicated (includes baseline infra + reserved capacity amortized). Will refine after projection run.

I'll schedule the infra run for Nov 17 morning and share updated numbers by EOD.

-jaz

Subject: BrightHealth — Maestro perf summary, recommended variant, and next steps

Emily / Mike / Procurement —

Quick recap and recommended path forward after the initial sweep and infra tuning run we did this morning:

Summary: rw-13b-q4 hits BrightHealth's accuracy target (QA exact match 81%) and, with the deployment configuration Jasmine ran (2-worker Dedicated pool, prefix caching, adaptive batching), shows production-like tail latency that meets your p95 <= 300ms SLO in our tests (measured p95 ~230ms, TTFT ~58ms) while sustaining ~600 tokens/sec at concurrency 12. The rw-3b-int8 is attractive for cost-limited workloads but misses QA targets. rw-70b-8q gives better quality but cannot meet latency/concurrency SLO without expensive sharding.

Proposal:
- Move to a pilot on Dedicated using rw-13b-q4 with a 2-week pilot window. Pilot scope: integration, safety checks, 2M tokens simulated traffic, and cost report.
- Commercial: draft term sheet attached (proposal_terms_BH_v1.pdf). Suggested pricing: usage + 12-month reserved Dedicated discount (we can discuss any procurement clauses you need).
- Timeline: pilot kickoff Nov 22, pilot wrap and exec review Dec 6, target production rollout in Dec (subject to procurement).

Action items for BrightHealth:
1) Confirm pilot kickoff date (we've penciled Nov 22).
2) Share procurement questionnaire answers (SOC2 evidence — we'll provide a SOC2 packet link).
3) Confirm dataset package for the pilot (finalized by Nov 19 preferred).

If you want, we can run a short live demo for your execs on Nov 19 showing the 2-worker rw-13b-q4 demo with real traffic and tracing dashboards. Please let me know which time window works.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
